definition: The browser API for building immersive VR and AR experiences.
A fully synthetic stereo scene that replaces the user's view ('immersive-vr').
Virtual content composited over the real world via passthrough or see-through optics ('immersive-ar').
A non-immersive XR session rendered inside a normal page element.
A coordinate system XRFrame poses are reported in (local, local-floor, bounded-floor, unbounded, viewer).
A reference space whose origin sits on the floor beneath the user.
A floor-level space bounded by a polygon the user defined (their play area).
Six degrees of freedom: tracked position and rotation.
Three degrees of freedom: rotation only, no positional tracking.
Interpupillary distance — the spacing between the eyes, used to set up the stereo cameras.
The angular extent of the scene visible through the headset optics.
Rendering the periphery at lower resolution to save GPU; see renderer.xr.setFoveation().
Warping the last rendered frame to the latest head pose to hide dropped frames (a.k.a. spacewarp).
Showing the headset's camera feed of the real world behind virtual content.
The play-area boundary system that warns the user before they leave a safe space.
An AR query that intersects a ray with detected real-world geometry.
A pose that the runtime keeps fixed to a point in the real world as tracking refines.
Detecting real-world planar surfaces (floors, walls, tables) as XRPlane objects.
Reconstructing a triangle mesh of the real environment.
Per-pixel real-world depth, used for occlusion of virtual objects.
